conventions.convention: Natural units c = ℏ = 1; spacetime R^(1,3) has metric diag(−1,1,1,1). Chiral fields have engineering dimension one, and their physical scalar, spinor and auxiliary components have dimensions 1, 3/2 and 2.
Physical brackets are [U]_D = −I_D(U)/4 and [Y]_F = I_F(Y)/2. Physical components satisfy ψ_raw = √2 ψ and F_raw = 2F; Hermitian conjugation is added once to the extracted F coefficient.

Operator quotients, ordered bases, light fields and the holomorphic coordinate projection remain fixed and unrescaled during cutoff evolution. Nonrenormalization is conditional on the specified formal background-jet extension, Ward identities, locality, one-particle-irreducible vertex prescription and absence of a local gauge anomaly.

Threshold matching retains only degree zero in the formal superspace-derivative expansion, with spacetime derivatives of degree one and D and barred D of degree one-half. M > 0 is the declared physical threshold mass. No discarded-term bound or full amplitude match follows from this projection.
Wilsonian scale, renormalization scale, threshold mass, external-energy scale, regulator cutoff and operator-suppression scale are distinct supplied inputs unless additional model data identify them.

The example fixes a nondynamical chiral spurion with raw top coefficient 2F_X. Its soft scalar trilinear terminology means a scalar cubic with a positive-mass-dimension coefficient; no numerical smallness or protection after supersymmetry breaking is claimed.

load_bearing.statement: Defines finite-order local rigid N=1 Wilsonian action data with separate holomorphic F and real D sectors, a declared finite operator quotient and representatives, optional conditional on-shell equivalence data, and finite threshold matching data with separately supplied scales.

For W_+(Φ,X) = W_L(Φ) + MX²/2 + XJ(Φ), with M > 0 and the stated canonical-heavy-field, tree-level degree-zero elimination prescription, W_-^(0)(Φ) = W_L(Φ) − J(Φ)²/(2M). This supplies only the leading derivative-free holomorphic coefficient component, not the selected amplitude matching conditions.

Under the stated formal perturbative cutoff, background-jet, Ward-identity, locality, one-particle-irreducibility and anomaly-free hypotheses, with fixed unrescaled fields and scale-independent projection, P_hol W_λ = P_hol W_Λ₀ coefficientwise at every perturbative order. Gauge-kinetic coefficients may receive one-loop corrections; real D-term data are not protected.

concerns.concern: The reference labels describe full Choice as 'required by the conditional operator-equivalence input' and call the equivalence theorem 'Full-AC conditional'. The current thm-aqft-field-redefinition-observable-equivalence-at-fixed-order has no full-Choice premise or proof use: its coordinate changes, Jacobians, overlap matrices and residue roots are supplied data. The finite quotient supplier likewise does not require full Choice. The same attribution recurs in the nonrenormalization theorem's A1 ('the selected invariant-quotient/on-shell-equivalence input uses it') and in the threshold/example inheritance explanations. Adopting full Choice as an additional assumption is harmless, but attributing its necessity to these current suppliers is inaccurate.

seams_checked.note: The consumer preserves the supplier's formal background-jet, Ward-identity, derivative-expansion, one-particle-irreducibility and anomaly hypotheses. Setting W = 0 removes all collected quadratic gauge terms before applying the fixed projection. The source argument was also checked in [Weinberg, equations (1)–(12)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/hep-th/9803099).
This is an inherited page prerequisite through the Ward/nonrenormalization page. The assigned items invoke no extended-supersymmetry action theorem and make only rigid N=1 claims.

The consumer retains selected amplitudes, common infrared regulation, supplied truncations and distinct scales. It explicitly leaves amplitude equality to be checked and does not claim RG compatibility from the superpotential substitution.

The physical brackets, component conversions and ordered projector agree with the normalization supplier. The threshold proof includes the additional real D-term variation before taking degree zero; its canonical chiral variation is consistent with [Martin, §4.7](https://arxiv.org/pdf/hep-ph/9709356v7).

Finite jet/degree/weight/loop cutoffs, declared relation spaces and representatives are retained. Neither a complete physical operator classification nor off-shell or scattering equivalence is inferred from the quotient alone.

The substantive optional equivalence hypotheses are preserved, but the claim that full Choice is required by the current equivalence theorem is inaccurate: that theorem states no such premise. See the presentation concern on def-aqft-susy-wilsonian-action.

Smooth classical chiral fields, ordered Grassmann extraction and nonnegative formal derivative degrees are used consistently. Compact-support or vanishing-boundary assumptions are supplied for integration by parts.

Ordered extraction gives raw top coefficient 2F_X φ³; the physical half-bracket gives the displayed trilinear. The nonzero-F_X supersymmetry-breaking conclusion and zero-F_X exception are explicit. The spurion construction agrees with [Martin, equations (7.6.1)–(7.6.5)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/hep-ph/9709356v7).
